It also suggests a fallback race plan: run as long as she comfortably can, then walk for a minute. The plan keeps to her Mon/Wed/Sat routine and starts gently with 7 x 2 min run / 1 min walk. Sessions of 21–25 min, much of it walking, are in line with the 5–7 km weeks she did before, so there's no sharp jump. It notes her driving stiffness and keeps her dog walks. Thursday is a backup day if Wednesday slips, and it asks her to report back on Saturday. Each day can be run as written. It loses a point because going up to 4-minute run bits within the first week back, after an on-off month, is a little quick for a new runner. Also, calling a 25-minute walk-run "long" overstates it, and the race-day progression table doesn't fully show in what came through.
